summary: Sound, rules-clean fusion that removes a measured 286.6-297.2 us act_and_mul_kernel per first_turn shape plus about 270 MB of round-trip traffic, and prepare()'s existing Triton-vs-Marlin e2e check gates its correctness. The headline gain is about 0.6-0.7%, below the drift floor, so judge it on the act_and_mul row disappearing and the _moe_nvfp4_gemm_kernel row (8149-8873 us) not growing. The main risk is register and shared-memory pressure in the BLOCK_T 256 w13 epilogue, which already spills.
justification: Mechanism: in master's profile (fb1e52d2119d4175) act_and_mul_kernel is 297.2 / 287.3 / 286.6 / 287.4 us on the four first_turn shapes (1.3-2.0% of each), and it runs at 14-53 us on the turn shapes, which stay on Marlin and are untouched. Fusing it into the w13 epilogue drops that launch. It also drops the bf16 write and re-read of the [~16K local slots, 8192] gate|up tensor (about 268 MB each way) and halves the w13 store to 134 MB. The claim of about 300-400 us off each first_turn shape is plausible. The permutation is lossless and keeps the codes NVFP4: whole rows of codes and block scales move, and the per-expert global scale is unchanged. Numerics: rounding acc*gs to bf16 before silu reproduces today's bf16 cache1 path, so the result matches SGLang's act_and_mul to within its own fp32 silu ordering. Expected directions are consistent with TASK.md. first_turn carries 186 of the load's shape weight (138 sliding plus 3 x 16 full), about 2.86 s per load. 300 us x 186 is about 56 ms, about 1.9-2.0% on the first_turn load. The headline is a geomean over three loads with turn_1 and turn_4 flat, so it moves only about 0.6-0.7% (1.060 to about 1.067), inside the CI [1.044, 1.076] and under LESSONS' 1.5-2.5% drift floor. The hypothesis says this itself and correctly says to read the kernel rows instead. Weakest link: the epilogue cost at BLOCK_T 256. The prepare log already shows the w13 BLOCK_T=256 variant at n_regs=254 with n_spills=4 and shared=140288 B. With 8 warps and BLOCK_W=128, Triton's wgmma layout most likely puts rows 0-63 (gate) in warpgroup 0 and rows 64-127 (up) in warpgroup 1. The reshape(2,64,BLOCK_T)/permute/split would then force a convert_layout of the 128x256 fp32 accumulator (128 KB) through shared memory, plus sigmoid temporaries on top of an already-spilling register file. The w13 GEMM is about 2/3 of the 8.1-8.9 ms row, about 5.5 ms. A 5% slowdown from extra spills or the smem round-trip would cancel the whole ~300 us. This cannot cause a correctness failure, only a null or negative result.
confounders: experts-triton-w4a16-first-turn-blockt256 (landed, stage 3): it set BLOCK_T=256, 8 warps and 2 stages, the config whose 254 regs and 4 spills the fused epilogue must fit in. A gain or loss in the _moe_nvfp4_gemm_kernel row is partly an interaction with that tile choice. At BLOCK_T 128 the same epilogue would be far cheaper but the GEMM slower. This shapes the result's magnitude but does not make it ambiguous: the act_and_mul row and the GEMM row are read separately.

experts-hybrid-marlin-turn-triton-first-turn (landed, stage 4): its shape gate confines the change to T > 4096, so the turn shapes are a built-in null control. If the gate were absent, the fused path would also run at turn_1 and turn_4, at BLOCK_T 64 and 128 with much smaller acc. No interaction on the shapes this run touches.

sglang-pipeline-parity (landed): it supplies the silu_and_mul semantics being replaced (gate first, then up, bf16 in and out, -1 slots skipped). No timing interaction beyond defining the reference behaviour.
interference: No companion is warranted. Both outcomes can be read from this one run's own profile. Gain: act_and_mul_kernel disappears from the first_turn shapes and the _moe_nvfp4_gemm_kernel row grows by less than about 290 us. Loss: that row grows by more than the saved time, which the prepare log's n_regs, n_spills and shared lines for the FUSE_SILU w13 variant will explain. A FUSE_SILU_W13=False control with the permuted bank would be master's kernel with a lossless row permutation and teaches nothing beyond the profile. An ab-revert of stage 3 (BLOCK_T 128 at first_turn) would ask a different tuning question. Checks are spent and this is a scored submit, so spending more runs on an expected ~0.65% headline is not justified.
rules_flags: None blocking. The w13 code and scale row permutation is a lossless repack in prepare() and the codes stay NVFP4. There is no BF16 weight copy and dequant stays in registers, as the user ruled.
Keep the specified bf16 rounding of acc*gs before silu. The activation stays BF16 where SGLang keeps BF16 (cache1), and dropping that rounding would quietly change the numerical path.
No host sync, no input-value branching. FUSE_SILU is a constexpr and the path choice depends only on x.shape[0].
open_questions: Correctness gating for a scored submit: none of the 5 judge tests exceeds 4096 tokens, so the fused path runs only in the timed first_turn calls. Make sure _check_experts_e2e (T=8192, rel L2 <= 2e-2 vs Marlin) actually runs the FUSE_SILU=True path. Also consider adding a direct fused-epilogue assertion in _check_expert_gemms: silu(bf16(ref_g)) * bf16(ref_u) at the permuted rows, checking the column mapping pid_w*64 + arange(64), the -1 block untouched and the past-n_padded block untouched. A layout bug then fails in prepare with a precise message rather than through the e2e tolerance.

The output tensor is [num_slots, 4096], but the kernel uses N (8192 for w13) for both the weight row count and the C row stride. The fused store needs its own output stride (N // 2) and column base pid_w * (BLOCK_W // 2). Easy to miss.

Could a finer gate/up interleave avoid the cross-warpgroup convert_layout? For example, 8 gate rows then 8 up rows in each 16-row slab, so each thread's wgmma accumulator pair (rows r, r+8) holds g and u. Check the TTGIR or the shared/n_spills numbers: if the 128-row/64-row split forces a 128 KB smem shuffle and more spills, that is the first thing to change.

Merge order with the queued p1 experts-triton-nvfp4-packed-asm-dequant: both edit _moe_nvfp4_gemm_kernel, and the register budget the epilogue sees depends on which lands first. Re-read n_spills after any 3-way merge.

silu_and_mul skips -1 slots and the fused path never writes them. cache2's -1 rows stay uninitialized, as today, and w2's -1 blocks never read A. Confirm the new separate cache2 allocation is not read anywhere else, e.g. by the post-expert norm, which reads y with slot_expert_ids.
